EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A "historic agreement" for the complete disarmament of Hamas in Gaza was announced by US President Donald Trump, though details remain disputed with Hamas officials. Simultaneously, direct hostilities between Iran and the US/Israel have significantly escalated with Iranian drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, and US/Saudi strikes against targets in Iraq and Iran, including a civilian residence on Qeshm Island.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran included US/Saudi airstrikes in Iraq's Diyala province, which resulted in the repatriation of five deceased IRGC members via the Mehran border. A US attack on Qeshm Island reportedly struck a residential home, killing a family of three (Qeysar Jafari, Zahra Jafari, and their two-year-old son Sina) and injuring two other children. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf condemned this as a "terrorist attack on civilians" and vowed "the perpetrators will pay the price." US/Israeli strikes were also reported on Shajareh Tayyebeh School in Minab.

In retaliation, the Iranian Army launched drone attacks on US military assets in Kuwait, specifically targeting fighter jet shelters, satellite communication systems, and equipment depots at Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in what was described as the 27th phase of Operation Sa'eqeh. Further Iranian strikes, identified as the 26th phase of Operation Thunder, hit the US Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain. The IRGC also claimed to have struck and halted two US-backed tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, forcing four others to change course, and asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is closed without IRGC Navy coordination. This claim was directly refuted by CENTCOM. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi denied Iranian involvement in a recent drone attack on ships at Egypt's Damietta Port, warning against Israeli "false-flag operations."

Internally, President Trump suggested the Iranian regime might eventually fall due to internal divisions following the January 2025 killings. Economically, Saudi Arabia's economy recorded its sharpest quarterly contraction since the COVID-19 pandemic, attributed to the war with Iran disrupting oil exports. Oil company profits reportedly increased due to market disruptions.

ISRAEL
The IDF conducted a strike in southern Gaza, eliminating Ahmed Hussein Mohammed Kafina, a top commander in the Mujahideen Brigades terror group. Kafina was implicated in the October 7, 2023, raid and the abduction of Avinatan Or, Noa Argamani, and Sudthisak Rinthalak. The IDF justified the strike by stating Kafina posed an "immediate threat" and planned attacks. Overnight, the Israeli Air Force bombed four Hamas weapon depots across the Gaza Strip, destroying sites storing assault rifles, explosive devices, and anti-tank missile launchers. Brigade 188 completed its eight-month mission in southern Gaza, destroying over ten Hamas tunnel routes, one of which was used for holding hostages.

In the West Bank, IDF forces carried out operations in Beit Oumer, scanning over 170 locations, arresting wanted individuals, and locating various weapons. In Tubas, 10 pipe bombs were located and destroyed. Near Misad in the Etzion Brigade area, a Palestinian who allegedly attempted to seize a weapon from a security coordinator was shot in the leg and detained. A vehicle that accelerated towards IDF troops in the Beit Hagot villages of Samaria was neutralized, with the driver being shot, resulting in no Israeli casualties.

On the home front, residents of the Upper Galilee were notified to open windows due to an anticipated large blast from IDF activity in Lebanon. Politically, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz announced the IDF's demolition of Hezbollah's tunnel system in Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon. Netanyahu returned from the US, landing at Nevatim Air Base for security reasons. Knesset Member Yulia Malinovsky advocated for right-wing control of the Justice and Defense ministries in the next government. The Defense Minister announced the cancellation of planned cuts to community defense in the Gaza envelope. Netanyahu reiterated Israel's demand for complete Hamas disarmament and demilitarization as a prerequisite for any political process in Gaza, denying that the Gaza issue was directly discussed with President Trump.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, the IDF killed Ahmed Hussein Mohammed Kafina, a Mujahideen Brigades commander involved in the October 7 abductions, and destroyed four Hamas weapons depots. Brigade 188 concluded operations in southern Gaza, neutralizing Hamas tunnel infrastructure including one used for hostages. The humanitarian situation remains dire, with most of Gaza's two million residents living in temporary shelters despite increased aid.

Regarding the ceasefire and negotiations, US President Donald Trump announced a "historic agreement" by the "Peace Council" for the "complete disarmament of Hamas and all armed groups in Gaza." This agreement reportedly involves a new Palestinian government collaborating with the Peace Council, a phased Israeli withdrawal, and a new Palestinian police force supported by an international stabilization force assuming security control. However, senior Hamas official Ghazi Hamad stated that Hamas would not disarm before a full Israeli withdrawal from the Gaza Strip, and insisted that heavy weapons would be transferred to a "National Committee for Gaza Management" without Israeli involvement, contradicting the US-announced phased disarmament. Negotiations continue in Cairo, focusing on the storage of heavy weapons under Palestinian supervision in exchange for IDF withdrawal, with a timeline of 6-8 months for the full process. Israel's War Cabinet Minister Gadi Eisenkot emphasized that any agreement must achieve the war's objectives of destroying or dismantling Hamas's military and governmental power, or it would be a "complete failure." Former Defense Minister Avigdor Lieberman criticized the emerging agreement as a return to the pre-October 7 security conception.

In the West Bank, Israeli settlers conducted an unapproved "tour" into the outskirts of Nablus, including areas A and B, where they reportedly vandalized a cemetery and clashed with Palestinians. An Israeli fired into the air, and later, the IDF engaged with Palestinian stone-throwers, shooting a "main instigator." The IDF emphasized that entry into Area A is prohibited and dangerous for Israeli civilians.

LEBANON
Hezbollah violated the ceasefire by targeting an unmanned bulldozer with an explosive drone. In response, the IDF carried out a significant operation, demolishing Hezbollah's extensive tunnel system beneath Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon, using approximately 700 tons of explosives. This infrastructure was described as a central command complex for Hezbollah's 'Badr' unit, funded and planned by Iran, and was located about 6 kilometers from Metula. The IDF is still monitoring another major Hezbollah tunnel system beneath the Ali Taher ridge, where dozens of operatives are believed to be present. Reports also indicate Israeli artillery fire in Tallouse, Haltah, Shama, and Shihin in southern Lebanon, and a drone attack in Nabatiyeh.

SYRIA & IRAQ
US/Saudi airstrikes in Iraq's Diyala province resulted in the death of five IRGC members. A drone attacked a camp of Iranian-Kurdish opposition forces in northern Iraq, near Erbil, with multiple explosions targeting separatist camps in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah. Saudi Arabia launched airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled capital of Yemen, Sanaa. The Iraqi government spokesperson denied authorizing the US and Saudi strikes and stated a lack of prior information on these operations. Syria's President Ahmed al-Shara affirmed his country's full support for Saudi Arabia's security and stability.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's economy experienced its sharpest quarterly contraction since the COVID-19 pandemic, attributed to the ongoing war with Iran. Riyadh is preparing for a large-scale military operation against Houthi forces in Yemen, involving potential sea and ground attacks in central Yemen, to break the Houthi blockade on Saudi oil exports. Saudi Arabia also announced a plan to form a multinational maritime coalition with 14 other nations (including Egypt, Jordan, Turkey, Pakistan, Kuwait, and Djibouti) to secure shipping lanes in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab, with its headquarters in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman met with US officials, emphasizing Riyadh's preference for de-escalation with Iran but stressing that attacks on Saudi infrastructure and energy constitute a "red line" requiring military response. Six Saudi tankers altered their course from Bab al-Mandab, possibly to bypass the Houthi threat by taking the longer route around Africa. US President Trump expressed optimism about finalizing a historic US-Saudi civil nuclear energy agreement.

The United Arab Emirates reportedly held secret meetings with Israel in a third country to coordinate their positions on Iran, expressing strong opposition to a perceived Iran-US understanding as a tactic for Iran to buy time. Kuwait confirmed that its armed forces detected and destroyed several hostile drones, identified as Iranian, which caused material damage to vital and military facilities, though no human casualties were reported. The Pentagon is reportedly considering a significant reduction of its permanent military presence in Kuwait dueage to repeated Iranian attacks. A US base in Bahrain, Sheikh Isa Air Base, was also struck by Iranian drones.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Gaza Disarmament Agreement**: US President Donald Trump announced a "historic agreement" for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all armed groups in Gaza by a "Peace Council," involving a new Palestinian government, phased Israeli withdrawal, and international/Palestinian police security.
2.  **Iranian Strikes on US Bases**: Iranian Army announced drone attacks on US Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base and Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, and Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, in retaliation for recent US attacks on Iran, including Qeshm Island.
3.  **US Strikes in Iran and Iraq**: US attacks targeted residential homes on Qeshm Island, killing a family of three (Qeysar Jafari, Zahra Jafari, and their two-year-old son Sina). US/Saudi airstrikes in Iraq's Diyala province killed five IRGC members.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions**: Iran's IRGC claimed to have struck and halted two US-backed tankers and forced four others to turn back in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting the Strait is closed without IRGC coordination. CENTCOM refuted these claims.
5.  **Hezbollah Tunnel Demolition**: The IDF destroyed Hezbollah's extensive tunnel system beneath Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon using approximately 700 tons of explosives, in response to Hezbollah's violation of the ceasefire.
6.  **Saudi Military Preparations in Yemen**: Saudi Arabia is preparing for a large-scale military operation against Houthi forces in Yemen, including potential sea and ground attacks, aimed at breaking the Houthi blockade on Saudi oil exports.
7.  **Israeli Settler Clashes in Nablus**: Unapproved incursions by Israeli settlers into the outskirts of Nablus led to clashes with Palestinians, vandalization of a cemetery, and an Israeli firing into the air. IDF intervened to remove the settlers.
8.  **Kuwaiti Military Presence Review**: The Pentagon is considering a significant reduction of its permanent military presence in Kuwait following repeated Iranian drone attacks on US bases in the country.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation remains high, marked by continued direct hostilities between Iran and the US/Israel. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where IRGC claims of control directly challenge international shipping; southern Lebanon, following the IDF's major tunnel demolition and ongoing monitoring of Hezbollah infrastructure; and Yemen, with Saudi Arabia's preparations for a large-scale offensive against Houthi forces. In the West Bank, unapproved settler incursions and clashes with Palestinians continue to fuel instability. Military postures are shifting, with Iran demonstrating retaliatory strike capabilities against US assets, the IDF maintaining high readiness and destroying Hezbollah infrastructure, and Saudi Arabia forming a maritime coalition while preparing for a Yemen offensive. The US Senate rejected limiting President Trump's military actions against Iran. Critical red lines include Iran's vow of retaliation for attacks on its territory or civilians, Saudi Arabia's assertion that attacks on its infrastructure are red lines necessitating military response, and Israel's zero-tolerance policy for Hezbollah ceasefire violations. The significant disagreement between Hamas's demand for full Israeli withdrawal before disarmament and the US-announced phased agreement highlights the fragility of the Gaza peace process.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is complex: President Trump announced a Gaza agreement, expressed public satisfaction, but privately conveyed frustration with the protracted conflict. He discussed a potential land blockade of Iran with Netanyahu and is seeking deeper military integration with Israel. The US Senate rejected limiting Trump's military action against Iran. Gulf states are actively responding: Saudi Arabia is forming a multinational maritime coalition and preparing for a major offensive in Yemen, while its Defense Minister emphasized de-escalation with Iran but firm deterrence. The UAE is reportedly coordinating with Israel against Iran and opposes the Iran-US understanding. Kuwait confirmed Iranian drone attacks and is seeing a potential reduction in US military presence. European nations, particularly Spain and Italy, are grappling with a massive influx of migrants into Ceuta, leading to diplomatic tensions and increased border security. China's military is integrating AI in defense, but Beijing denied reports of missile shipments to Iran. Turkey, a mediator in Gaza, advised Lebanon against rushing into an agreement with Israel. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry indicated ongoing Iran-US talks and urged restraint. Jordan's public figures called for US troop withdrawal following recent strikes. Iraq's government denied prior knowledge or authorization of US/Saudi strikes on its territory.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions emerge regarding the Gaza disarmament agreement, with President Trump's definitive announcement immediately countered by Hamas's insistence on Israeli withdrawal as a precondition for disarmament, and Israel's reiteration of full disarmament as a prerequisite. This suggests either a fundamental misunderstanding, an intentional ambiguity, or strategic posturing by the parties involved. Similarly, the IRGC's claims of striking tankers and closing the Strait of Hormuz are directly refuted by CENTCOM, indicating deliberate disinformation. The extent of damage to US bases from Iranian strikes, particularly claims of F-35 destruction, is highly unverified and denied by US and Kuwaiti authorities, although satellite imagery does show some material damage. Reports on Iran's role in the Damietta drone attack are conflicting, with some sources linking Iran and others, including Iranian and Egyptian officials, denying it. Unverified claims include the number and identities of IRGC members allegedly killed in Zanjan and specific US/Israeli strike locations in Iran like Minab. Propaganda is evident in the IRGC's dramatic and frequently disproven claims, as well as in Trump's highly optimistic statements about the Gaza agreement and Netanyahu's broad framing of the conflict. Reporting gaps include detailed information on the composition and authority of the "Peace Council" in Gaza, specific timetables for withdrawal or disarmament, and independent verification of many claimed casualties and damages.
